subproblem.title: Regularity and support of the initial velocity and acceleration of admissible deformations (Simon 5.1-5.2)
subproblem.statement: For every N ∈ ℕ, U, K ⊆ ℝᴺ (ℝᴺ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N)) and φ : ℝ → ℝᴺ → ℝᴺ: (a) if IsAdmissibleDeformation 2 U K φ (U open, K compact ⊆ U, (t, x) ↦ φ t x of class C² on (−1,1) × U, φ 0 = id on U, φ t x = x for t ∈ (−1,1) and x ∉ K, each φ t a bijection of U with bijective derivative on U), then the initial velocity X = initialVelocity φ, X(x) = d/dt φ(t,x)|_{t=0}, is C¹ on ℝᴺ and X(x) = 0 for x ∉ K; (b) if IsAdmissibleDeformation 3 U K φ, then X is C² on ℝᴺ, the initial acceleration Z = initialAcceleration φ, Z(x) = d/dt[d/ds φ(s,x)|_{s=t}]|_{t=0}, is C¹ on ℝᴺ, and X(x) = Z(x) = 0 for x ∉ K.
subproblem.lean_statement: (∀ (N : ℕ) (U K : Set (Rn N)) (φ : ℝ → Rn N → Rn N), IsAdmissibleDeformation 2 U K φ → ContDiff ℝ 1 (initialVelocity φ) ∧ ∀ x ∉ K, initialVelocity φ x = 0) ∧ ∀ (N : ℕ) (U K : Set (Rn N)) (φ : ℝ → Rn N → Rn N), IsAdmissibleDeformation 3 U K φ → ContDiff ℝ 2 (initialVelocity φ) ∧ ContDiff ℝ 1 (initialAcceleration φ) ∧ ∀ x ∉ K, initialVelocity φ x = 0 ∧ initialAcceleration φ x = 0
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon, Introduction to GMT, Ch. 2, 5.1-5.2 (pp. 61-62): X_x = ∂φ(t,x)/∂t|_{t=0} and Z_x = ∂²φ(t,x)/∂t²|_{t=0} "have supports which are compact subsets of U" (asserted without proof). This is step II.0′ of the parent proof, written out completely.

Setting. Let r ∈ {2, 3} and assume IsAdmissibleDeformation r U K φ: U ⊆ ℝᴺ is open, K is compact, K ⊆ U, Φ(t, x) := φ t x is C^r on O := (−1,1) × U, φ 0 x = x for x ∈ U, and φ t x = x whenever t ∈ (−1,1) and x ∉ K (the bijectivity clauses are not used). X := initialVelocity φ, X(x) = deriv (t ↦ φ t x) 0; Z := initialAcceleration φ, Z(x) = deriv (t ↦ deriv (s ↦ φ s x) t) 0. Put e := (1, 0) ∈ ℝ × ℝᴺ.

1. O is open. Since Φ is C^r on the open set O and r ≥ 2, DΦ = fderiv ℝ Φ is C^{r−1} on O and D²Φ = fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ Φ) is C^{r−2} on O (Mathlib ContDiffOn.fderiv_of_isOpen, applied once and twice).
2. Let x ∈ U and t ∈ (−1,1). Then (t, x) ∈ O and Φ is differentiable at (t, x) (C^r with r ≥ 1 on an open set). The map s ↦ φ s x equals Φ ∘ ι_x with ι_x(s) := (s, x), whose derivative is e. By the chain rule, s ↦ φ s x has derivative DΦ(t, x)e at t, so deriv (s ↦ φ s x) t = g(t, x) := DΦ(t, x)e. In particular X(x) = g(0, x) for x ∈ U.
3. g = (evaluation at e) ∘ DΦ is C^{r−1} on O, because evaluation at the fixed vector e is a continuous linear map. The map j : x ↦ (0, x) is smooth and maps U into O. Hence X = g ∘ j is C^{r−1} on U.
4. Let x ∈ U. The functions t ↦ deriv (s ↦ φ s x) t and t ↦ g(t, x) coincide on (−1,1), an open neighbourhood of 0 (step 2), so they have the same derivative at 0 (Filter.EventuallyEq.deriv_eq). By the chain rule with ι_x, the derivative of t ↦ g(t, x) at 0 is Dg(0, x)e = D²Φ(0, x)(e)(e). Hence Z(x) = D²Φ(0, x) e e for x ∈ U, and Z is C^{r−2} on U (D²Φ is C^{r−2} on O, double evaluation at e is continuous linear, and we compose with j).
5. K is compact in a Hausdorff space, hence closed, so Kᶜ is open. Let x ∉ K. For every t ∈ (−1,1) the function s ↦ φ s x is constant (= x) on the neighbourhood (−1,1) of t, so deriv (s ↦ φ s x) t = 0. Taking t = 0 gives X(x) = 0. Moreover t ↦ deriv (s ↦ φ s x) t vanishes on the neighbourhood (−1,1) of 0, so its derivative at 0 is 0: Z(x) = 0. Thus X ≡ 0 and Z ≡ 0 on the open set Kᶜ, and they are C^∞ there.
6. Since K ⊆ U, U ∪ Kᶜ = ℝᴺ. Every point of ℝᴺ has an open neighbourhood (U or Kᶜ) on which X is C^{r−1} and Z is C^{r−2}; ContDiffOn on an open set gives ContDiffAt at each of its points, and ContDiff ℝ k F ↔ ∀ x, ContDiffAt ℝ k F x (contDiff_iff_contDiffAt). Hence X is C^{r−1} and Z is C^{r−2} on ℝᴺ, and X(x) = Z(x) = 0 for x ∉ K by step 5.
7. Conclusion. With r = 2 (the numeral (2 : ℕ∞) coerced to WithTop ℕ∞): ContDiff ℝ 1 X and X(x) = 0 for x ∉ K, the first conjunct. With r = 3: ContDiff ℝ 2 X, ContDiff ℝ 1 Z, and X(x) = Z(x) = 0 for x ∉ K, the second conjunct.
proof_key_steps: Φ(t,x) = φ t x is C^r on the open set (−1,1) × U, so DΦ is C^{r−1} and D²Φ is C^{r−2} there.
On U, chain rule: X(x) = DΦ(0,x)(1,0) and, since t ↦ ∂_sφ(s,x)|_{s=t} agrees with DΦ(t,x)(1,0) near 0, Z(x) = D²Φ(0,x)(1,0)(1,0); so X ∈ C^{r−1}(U), Z ∈ C^{r−2}(U).
Off the closed set K, t ↦ φ_t(x) is constant on (−1,1), so X = Z = 0 on the open set Kᶜ.
U ∪ Kᶜ = ℝᴺ and ContDiff is local, giving global C^{r−1}/C^{r−2}; specialise r = 2 and r = 3.

subproblem.title: Hausdorff measure of compact and relatively open pieces of a Simon submanifold
subproblem.statement: Let n, N ∈ ℕ, r ∈ ℕ∞ and M ⊆ ℝᴺ an n-dimensional C^r Simon submanifold (Chapter02.IsSimonSubmanifold (E := ℝⁿ) r M, which includes r ≥ 1). Then (a) μHE[n](C) < ∞ for every compact C ⊆ M, and (b) μHE[n](M ∩ O) > 0 for every y ∈ M and every open O ⊆ ℝᴺ with y ∈ O.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n N : ℕ) (r : ℕ∞) (M : Set (Rn N)), Chapter02.IsSimonSubmanifold (E := Rn n) r M → (∀ C ⊆ M, IsCompact C → μHE[n] C < ⊤) ∧ ∀ y ∈ M, ∀ O : Set (Rn N), IsOpen O → y ∈ O → 0 < μHE[n] (M ∩ O)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: the finiteness hypothesis "Hⁿ(K ∩ M) < ∞ for each compact K ⊂ U" of Simon Ch. 2, §5 (pp. 61-63), and the parent proof (II.1 step 3, II.2 steps 4 and 7), where these two facts are used; proved here completely.

Setting. M ⊆ ℝᴺ with IsSimonSubmanifold (E := ℝⁿ) r M: r ≥ 1 and every y ∈ M lies in W for some chart (V, W, ψ) of class r (V ⊆ ℝⁿ, W ⊆ ℝᴺ open, ψ C^r, hence C¹, on V, injective on V, ψ(V) = W ∩ M, relatively proper: V ∩ ψ⁻¹(K) is compact for every compact K ⊆ W, Dψ(x) injective for x ∈ V). Hⁿ := μHE[n].

Preliminaries.
(P1) On every metric space, μHE[n] = c_n · μH[n] with the same constant c_n := addHaarScalarFactor (volume on EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) μH[n] ∈ (0, ∞), which is defined through the model space ℝⁿ and therefore does not depend on the ambient space (definition Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure; addHaarScalarFactor_volume_hausdorffMeasure_ne_zero; it is finite since it is an NNReal). Hence, if f is K-Lipschitz on s, then μHE[n](f(s)) ≤ Kⁿ μHE[n](s) (LipschitzOnWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le with d = n, multiplied by c_n). On ℝⁿ, μHE[n] is Lebesgue measure (EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume), so bounded subsets of ℝⁿ have finite μHE[n]-measure.
(P2) If ψ is C¹ on the open set V and x ∈ V, choose δ > 0 with B̄(x, δ) ⊆ V. Dψ is continuous on the compact set B̄(x, δ), so K_x := sup over B̄(x, δ) of ‖Dψ‖ is finite, and by the mean value inequality on the convex ball (Convex.lipschitzOnWith_of_nnnorm_fderiv_le) ψ is K_x-Lipschitz on B(x, δ). (Alternatively ContDiffAt.exists_lipschitzOnWith.)

(a) Compact subsets of M have finite Hⁿ-measure.
1. Let C ⊆ M be compact. For each y ∈ C choose a chart (V_y, W_y, ψ_y) of class r with y ∈ W_y, and ρ_y > 0 with B̄(y, ρ_y) ⊆ W_y (W_y is open). The open balls B(y, ρ_y), y ∈ C, cover C; choose y_1, …, y_p with C ⊆ ⋃_q B(y_q, ρ_q). Then C = ⋃_q C_q with C_q := C ∩ B̄(y_q, ρ_q), each compact and contained in W_q := W_{y_q}.
2. Fix q and write (V, W, ψ) := (V_{y_q}, W_q, ψ_{y_q}). By relative properness, Q := V ∩ ψ⁻¹(C_q) is compact. Since C_q ⊆ M ∩ W = ψ(V), every z ∈ C_q equals ψ(x) for some x ∈ V, and then x ∈ Q; hence C_q = ψ(Q).
3. By (P2) and compactness of Q, there are finitely many balls B(x_j, δ_j) ⊆ V (j = 1, …, m) covering Q such that ψ is K_j-Lipschitz on B(x_j, δ_j). By (P1), μHE[n](ψ(B(x_j, δ_j))) ≤ K_jⁿ · Lⁿ(B(x_j, δ_j)) < ∞. Since C_q = ψ(Q) ⊆ ⋃_j ψ(B(x_j, δ_j)), monotonicity and subadditivity give μHE[n](C_q) < ∞.
4. Hence μHE[n](C) ≤ Σ_q μHE[n](C_q) < ∞.
(Alternative for step 3: by the SimonGMT area formula IsSimonLocalRepresentation.area_formula, μHE[n](ψ(Q)) = ∫_Q Jψ dLⁿ, and the continuous function Jψ = areaJacobianAt ψ is bounded on the compact Q, while Lⁿ(Q) < ∞.)

(b) Relatively open pieces of M have positive Hⁿ-measure.
5. Let y ∈ M and O ⊆ ℝᴺ open with y ∈ O. Choose a chart (V, W, ψ) of class r with y ∈ W; since y ∈ W ∩ M = ψ(V), y = ψ(x₀) for some x₀ ∈ V. Because ψ is continuous on the open set V, V′ := V ∩ ψ⁻¹(O ∩ W) is open (ContinuousOn.isOpen_inter_preimage) and contains x₀. Moreover ψ(V′) ⊆ O ∩ (W ∩ M) ⊆ M ∩ O.
6. By the SimonGMT area formula for charts, IsSimonLocalRepresentation.area_formula (applicable since r ≥ 1 and V′ is a measurable subset of V), μHE[finrank ℝ ℝⁿ](ψ(V′)) = ∫⁻_{V′} ENNReal.ofReal(Jψ(x)) dLⁿ(x), where Jψ(x) = areaJacobianAt ψ x = normDet(Dψ(x)); and finrank ℝ ℝⁿ = n (finrank_euclideanSpace_fin).
7. For x ∈ V′, Dψ(x) is injective, so normDet(Dψ(x)) ≠ 0 (LinearMap.normDet_ne_zero_tfae), hence Jψ(x) > 0 (normDet ≥ 0). The function x ↦ ofReal(Jψ(x)) is measurable (SimonGMT measurable_areaJacobianAt) and strictly positive on V′, and Lⁿ(V′) > 0 because V′ is a nonempty open set (IsOpen.measure_pos). A lintegral over V′ of a measurable function vanishes only if the function vanishes a.e. on V′, which is impossible here; so ∫⁻_{V′} ofReal(Jψ) dLⁿ > 0.
8. By monotonicity of the outer measure μHE[n], μHE[n](M ∩ O) ≥ μHE[n](ψ(V′)) > 0.
(No case distinction on n is needed: for n = 0, ℝ⁰ is a single point of Lebesgue measure 1 and the normDet of a map out of the zero space is 1.)
proof_key_steps: Cover a compact C ⊆ M by finitely many compact pieces C_q = C ∩ B̄(y_q, ρ_q) inside chart targets; C_q = ψ_q(Q_q) with Q_q compact by relative properness.
ψ_q is locally Lipschitz (C¹), so μHE[n](ψ_q(Q_q)) ≤ Σ_j K_jⁿ Lⁿ(B_j) < ∞; sum over q.
For y = ψ(x₀) ∈ M ∩ O, V′ := V ∩ ψ⁻¹(O ∩ W) is a nonempty open set with ψ(V′) ⊆ M ∩ O.
Area formula: μHE[n](ψ(V′)) = ∫_{V′} Jψ dLⁿ > 0 because Jψ > 0 (Dψ injective) and Lⁿ(V′) > 0.

audit.reason: The hypotheses and conclusions match. Compact chart preimages and finite Lipschitz covers prove finiteness; the area formula and positive Jacobian prove positivity. The argument covers dimension zero.

subproblem.title: Scaled vector fields generate admissible deformations
subproblem.statement: Let N ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝᴺ open and Y : ℝᴺ → ℝᴺ of class C² with compact support and tsupport Y ⊆ U. Then there is a real c > 0 such that φ t x := x + (c t) • Y(x) satisfies IsAdmissibleDeformation 2 U (tsupport Y) φ and initialVelocity φ x = c • Y(x) for every x.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N : ℕ) (U : Set (Rn N)) (Y : Rn N → Rn N), IsOpen U → ContDiff ℝ 2 Y → HasCompactSupport Y → tsupport Y ⊆ U → ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ IsAdmissibleDeformation 2 U (tsupport Y) (fun t x ↦ x + (c * t) • Y x) ∧ ∀ x, initialVelocity (fun t x ↦ x + (c * t) • Y x) x = c • Y x
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof II.2 step 6 (the test deformations φ_t(x) = x + λtζ(x)e). Simon's remark after 5.4 (p. 63), "by the first variation formula 5.3 this is equivalent to ∫_M div_M X dHⁿ = 0 whenever X is C¹ on U with support X a compact subset of U", presupposes that such deformations are admissible; this is proved here.

Setting. U ⊆ ℝᴺ open, Y : ℝᴺ → ℝᴺ of class C² with compact support, K := tsupport Y ⊆ U.

1. K is compact (HasCompactSupport Y means that tsupport Y is compact) and K ⊆ U. If x ∉ K then Y vanishes on the open neighbourhood Kᶜ of x, so Y(x) = 0 and DY(x) = 0.
2. DY is continuous (Y ∈ C²) and vanishes outside the compact set K (HasCompactSupport.fderiv), hence bounded: L := sup over x of ‖DY(x)‖ < ∞. Put c := 1/(L + 1) > 0, so that c·L < 1.
3. By the mean value inequality on the convex space ℝᴺ (lipschitzWith_of_nnnorm_fderiv_le), ‖Y(x) − Y(x′)‖ ≤ L‖x − x′‖ for all x, x′.
4. Define φ t x := x + (c t)•Y(x). Fix t ∈ (−1, 1) and put s := c t and κ := |s| L ≤ c L < 1, so φ t = id + s Y.
 (i) φ t is injective: if x + sY(x) = x′ + sY(x′), then ‖x − x′‖ = |s|·‖Y(x′) − Y(x)‖ ≤ κ‖x − x′‖, so x = x′.
 (ii) φ t is surjective onto ℝᴺ: for z ∈ ℝᴺ the map T_z(x) := z − sY(x) is κ-Lipschitz with κ < 1 on the complete space ℝᴺ, so it has a fixed point x (Banach fixed point theorem, ContractingWith.fixedPoint); then x + sY(x) = z.
 (iii) φ t x = x for every x ∉ K, since Y(x) = 0.
 (iv) BijOn (φ t) U U. MapsTo: let x ∈ U. If x ∉ K, then φ t x = x ∈ U. If x ∈ K and φ t x ∉ K, then by (iii) φ t (φ t x) = φ t x, so injectivity (i) gives φ t x = x ∈ K, a contradiction; hence φ t x ∈ K ⊆ U. InjOn: by (i). SurjOn: let z ∈ U and choose x with φ t x = z by (ii). If x ∉ K then z = φ t x = x, so x ∈ U; if x ∈ K then x ∈ U. In both cases z ∈ φ t '' U.
 (v) For every x, fderiv ℝ (φ t) x = id + s·DY(x) (derivative of a sum and of a constant multiple). If (id + s DY(x))v = 0 then ‖v‖ = |s|·‖DY(x)v‖ ≤ κ‖v‖, so v = 0. Thus fderiv ℝ (φ t) x is an injective linear endomorphism of the finite-dimensional space ℝᴺ, hence bijective (LinearMap.injective_iff_surjective).
5. Regularity: (t, x) ↦ x + (c t)•Y(x) is C² on ℝ × ℝᴺ (built from the C² maps p ↦ p.2, p ↦ c·p.1 and p ↦ Y(p.2) by addition and scalar multiplication), in particular ContDiffOn ℝ 2 on (−1,1) ×ˢ U.
6. φ 0 x = x + 0•Y(x) = x for every x, in particular for x ∈ U.
7. Steps 1, 4(iii), 4(iv), 4(v), 5 and 6 are exactly the clauses of IsAdmissibleDeformation 2 U K φ: U open, K compact, K ⊆ U, C² on (−1,1) × U, φ 0 = id on U, φ t x = x for t ∈ (−1,1) and x ∉ K, and for each t ∈ (−1,1), BijOn (φ t) U U and fderiv ℝ (φ t) x bijective for x ∈ U.
8. Initial velocity: for fixed x, t ↦ x + (c t)•Y(x) is affine in t with derivative c•Y(x), so initialVelocity φ x = deriv (t ↦ φ t x) 0 = c•Y(x). Together with c > 0 this proves the claim.
proof_key_steps: L := sup‖DY‖ < ∞ (compact support), c := 1/(L+1); Y is L-Lipschitz by the mean value inequality.
For |t| < 1, φ_t = id + ctY is injective (contraction estimate), surjective (Banach fixed point) and the identity off K.
A bijection of ℝᴺ fixing Kᶜ pointwise maps K into K, hence BijOn (φ t) U U; Dφ_t = I + ctDY is injective, hence bijective.
φ is C², φ_0 = id, and the initial velocity is c·Y.

subproblem.title: Second fundamental form in a C² chart (Simon 4.26 for the frame-free B)
subproblem.statement: Assume (TH). (TH) is the frozen statement of the sibling root.submanifold_tangent-a1, taken as an explicit hypothesis: (TH1) for every Simon local representation (V, W, ψ) of class r ≥ 1 of any M ⊆ ℝᴺ, tangentSpace M (ψ x) = range Dψ(x) for x ∈ V; (TH2) every n-dimensional C^r Simon submanifold of ℝᴺ is a measurable set on which y ↦ tangentProjection M y is continuous. Then for all n, N ∈ ℕ, M ⊆ ℝᴺ, every Simon local representation (V, W, ψ) of M of class 2 (Chapter02.IsSimonLocalRepresentation 2 M V W ψ, ψ : ℝⁿ → ℝᴺ), every x ∈ V and all a, b ∈ ℝⁿ: secondFundamentalForm M (ψ x) (Dψ(x)a) (Dψ(x)b) = normalPart M (ψ x) (D²ψ(x)[a, b]), where D²ψ(x)[a, b] = fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ ψ) x a b; i.e. B_{ψ(x)}(Dψ(x)a, Dψ(x)b) = (I − P_{ψ(x)}) D²ψ(x)[a, b].
subproblem.lean_statement: ((∀ (n N : ℕ) (r : ℕ∞) (M : Set (Rn N)) (V : Set (Rn n)) (W : Set (Rn N)) (ψ : Rn n → Rn N), 1 ≤ r → Chapter02.IsSimonLocalRepresentation r M V W ψ → ∀ x ∈ V, tangentSpace M (ψ x) = LinearMap.range (fderiv ℝ ψ x).toLinearMap) ∧ ∀ (n N : ℕ) (r : ℕ∞) (M : Set (Rn N)), Chapter02.IsSimonSubmanifold (E := Rn n) r M → MeasurableSet M ∧ ContinuousOn (tangentProjection M) M) → ∀ (n N : ℕ) (M : Set (Rn N)) (V : Set (Rn n)) (W : Set (Rn N)) (ψ : Rn n → Rn N), Chapter02.IsSimonLocalRepresentation 2 M V W ψ → ∀ x ∈ V, ∀ a b : Rn n, secondFundamentalForm M (ψ x) (fderiv ℝ ψ x a) (fderiv ℝ ψ x b) = normalPart M (ψ x) (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ ψ) x a b)
subproblem.natural_proof:
(TH) denotes the frozen statement of the sibling node root.submanifold_tangent-a1 (Submission.simon_submanifold_tangent_basics), taken here as an explicit hypothesis: (TH1) for all n, N, r ≥ 1, M ⊆ ℝᴺ and every Simon local representation (V, W, ψ) of M of class r, tangentSpace M (ψ x) = range Dψ(x) for every x ∈ V; (TH2) every n-dimensional C^r Simon submanifold M of ℝᴺ is a measurable set and y ↦ tangentProjection M y is continuous on M.
Notation. ℝ^d := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) (= Rn d); Hⁿ := μHE[n]. A chart of class r of M is a triple (V, W, ψ) with Chapter02.IsSimonLocalRepresentation r M V W ψ: V ⊆ ℝⁿ and W ⊆ ℝᴺ open, ψ C^r on V, ψ injective on V, ψ(V) = W ∩ M, ψ relatively proper (V ∩ ψ⁻¹(K) is compact for every compact K ⊆ W) and Dψ(x) injective for x ∈ V. For y ∈ M: T_y := tangentSpace M y, P_y := tangentProjection M y (orthogonal projection onto T_y), v^⊥ := normalPart M y v = v − P_y v, τ_i := tangentFrame M y i (an orthonormal basis of T_y), B_y(τ, η) := secondFundamentalForm M y τ η = (fderivWithin ℝ (tangentProjection M) M y τ) η, H(y) := meanCurvature M y = Σ_i B_y(τ_i, τ_i), div_M Y(y) := tangentialDivergence M Y y = Σ_i ⟨τ_i, DY(y)τ_i⟩, and D²ψ(x)[a, b] := fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ ψ) x a b (the derivative at x in direction a of x′ ↦ Dψ(x′)b).

Source: Simon, Ch. 2, 4.23-4.26 (pp. 59-60). Printed: for C² M the second fundamental form is B_y(τ, η) = −Σ_α (η · D_τ ν^α) ν^α (4.24) for local orthonormal normal fields ν^α; B_y(τ, τ) = γ̈(0)^⊥ for a C² curve γ in M with γ(0) = y, γ̇(0) = τ (4.25); "More generally, by a similar argument, if τ, η ∈ T_yM and φ : U → ℝ^{n+ℓ} is a C² mapping of a neighbourhood U of 0 in ℝ² such that φ(U) ⊂ M, φ(0) = y, ∂φ/∂x¹(0,0) = τ, ∂φ/∂x²(0,0) = η, then B_y(τ, η) = (∂²φ/∂x¹∂x²(0,0))^⊥" (4.26). Reading applied (contract docstring and README): B is the frame-free form B_y(τ, η) = (D_τP)(η) = fderivWithin ℝ P M y τ η, which equals 4.24 because P = I − Σ_α ν^α ⊗ ν^α. The statement proved here is 4.26 for the coordinate surface (s₁, s₂) ↦ ψ(x + s₁a + s₂b) of a chart; the argument is steps G0-G2 of the parent proof.

Setting. Assume (TH); only (TH1) is used: T_{ψ′(x)} = range Dψ′(x) for every Simon local representation (V′, W′, ψ′) of class r ≥ 1 and x ∈ V′. (V, W, ψ) is a chart of M ⊆ ℝᴺ of class 2: V ⊆ ℝⁿ and W ⊆ ℝᴺ open, ψ C² on V, injective on V, ψ(V) = W ∩ M, relatively proper, Dψ(x) injective for x ∈ V. No global submanifold hypothesis is needed. Notation: A(x) := Dψ(x) = fderiv ℝ ψ x; D²ψ(x)[a, b] := fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ ψ) x a b; P_z := tangentProjection M z; w^⊥ := normalPart M z w = w − P_z w; P := tangentProjection M as a map z ↦ P_z. Fix x₀ ∈ V, y₀ := ψ(x₀) and a, b ∈ ℝⁿ.

1. (Projection onto the range of an injective map; parent G0.) Let A : ℝⁿ → ℝᴺ be linear and injective. Then G := A*A is injective (A*Av = 0 ⇒ ‖Av‖² = ⟨v, A*Av⟩ = 0 ⇒ Av = 0 ⇒ v = 0), hence invertible, and Π(A) := A G⁻¹ A* satisfies Π(A)* = Π(A), Π(A)² = Π(A), Π(A)A = A and Π(A)w = 0 whenever w ⊥ range A (then A*w = 0). So Π(A) is the orthogonal projection onto range A. The set ℐ of injective A is open (it is {A : det(A*A) ≠ 0}) and Π is C^∞ on ℐ (A ↦ A*A is polynomial, inversion is smooth on the invertible operators, adjoint and composition are smooth). By (TH1) with r = 2, T_{ψ(x)} = range A(x) for every x ∈ V, hence P_{ψ(x)} = Π(A(x)) for x ∈ V. Since ψ is C² on the open set V, x ↦ A(x) is C¹ on V with values in ℐ.
2. (Local left inverse of ψ; parent G1.) Let T₀ := range A(x₀), a subspace of dimension n, and Q := T₀^⊥, of dimension N − n. Define Ξ : ℝⁿ × Q → ℝᴺ, Ξ(x, q) := ψ(x) + q. Ξ is C² on the open set V × Q and DΞ(x₀, 0)(a′, q) = A(x₀)a′ + q. This linear map is injective (A(x₀)a′ + q = 0 gives A(x₀)a′ = −q ∈ T₀ ∩ T₀^⊥ = {0}, so q = 0, and a′ = 0 because A(x₀) is injective) between spaces of equal dimension n + (N − n) = N, hence a continuous linear isomorphism. By the inverse function theorem for C² maps (Mathlib ContDiffAt.toOpenPartialHomeomorph) there is a partial homeomorphism e with e = Ξ on its open source, (x₀, 0) ∈ e.source, and e.symm differentiable (indeed C²) at y₀ = e(x₀, 0) (ContDiffAt.to_localInverse, or OpenPartialHomeomorph.contDiffAt_symm). Restrict e to the open set Σ := e.source ∩ (V × Q) ∋ (x₀, 0) (OpenPartialHomeomorph.restrOpen) and let Θ := Ξ(Σ), an open set containing y₀ (a partial homeomorphism maps open subsets of its source to open sets); Ξ maps Σ bijectively onto Θ with inverse e.symm on Θ. Define π(z) := (e.symm z).1 for every z ∈ ℝᴺ (through the global function e.symm). Then π(z) ∈ V for z ∈ Θ, π(y₀) = x₀, and π is differentiable at y₀; only this differentiability at the single point y₀ is used below.
3. V₀ := {x ∈ V : (x, 0) ∈ Σ} is open and contains x₀. For x ∈ V₀ we have Ξ(x, 0) = ψ(x), so ψ(x) ∈ Θ and e.symm(ψ(x)) = (x, 0), i.e. π(ψ(x)) = x.
4. (Localisation in M; Simon 4.2.) By SimonGMT IsSimonLocalRepresentation.exists_open_image_eq_inter (which uses the relative properness) there is an open W₀ ⊆ W with ψ(V₀) = W₀ ∩ M. Put O := Θ ∩ W₀: an open set containing y₀ (y₀ = ψ(x₀) ∈ ψ(V₀) ⊆ W₀ and y₀ ∈ Θ). If z ∈ M ∩ O, then z ∈ W₀ ∩ M = ψ(V₀), so z = ψ(x) with x ∈ V₀ and π(z) = x by step 3. Conversely ψ(V₀) ⊆ M ∩ O.
5. (Extension of P near y₀.) Define P̃ : ℝᴺ → (ℝᴺ →L[ℝ] ℝᴺ) by P̃(z) := Π(A(π(z))) (with any value for z ∉ Θ, e.g. built from Ring.inverse). Since π is differentiable at y₀ with π(y₀) = x₀ ∈ V, A is differentiable at x₀, and Π is differentiable at A(x₀) ∈ ℐ, the chain rule shows that P̃ is differentiable at y₀; let L₀ := DP̃(y₀). For z ∈ M ∩ O, z = ψ(x) with x = π(z) ∈ V₀ ⊆ V, so P̃(z) = Π(A(x)) = P_{ψ(x)} = P_z by step 1. Thus P = P̃ on M ∩ O, and O is a neighbourhood of y₀.
6. (Derivative of P within M.) P̃ has Fréchet derivative L₀ at y₀, hence also within M at y₀. Since P and P̃ agree on M ∩ O, a neighbourhood of y₀ within M, and at y₀ ∈ M, HasFDerivWithinAt P L₀ M y₀ (HasFDerivWithinAt.congr_of_eventuallyEq). In particular P is differentiable within M at y₀, so fderivWithin ℝ P M y₀ is also a derivative of P within M at y₀ (DifferentiableWithinAt.hasFDerivWithinAt). By HasFDerivWithinAt.unique_on, fderivWithin ℝ P M y₀ and L₀ agree on the tangent cone tangentConeAt ℝ M y₀.
7. (Chart directions lie in the tangent cone.) ψ has derivative A(x₀) at x₀ within V, and V is a neighbourhood of x₀, so tangentConeAt ℝ V x₀ = ℝⁿ (tangentConeAt_of_mem_nhds). By HasFDerivWithinAt.mapsTo_tangent_cone, A(x₀)a ∈ tangentConeAt ℝ (ψ '' V) y₀ ⊆ tangentConeAt ℝ M y₀ (tangentConeAt_mono, since ψ '' V = W ∩ M ⊆ M). [Directly: c_k := k and d_k := ψ(x₀ + a/k) − y₀ satisfy y₀ + d_k ∈ M for large k, d_k → 0 and c_k d_k → A(x₀)a.] Hence, by step 6, for every η ∈ ℝᴺ: B_{y₀}(A(x₀)a, η) = fderivWithin ℝ P M y₀ (A(x₀)a) η = L₀(A(x₀)a) η.
8. (Computation of L₀; parent G2.) Let F(x) := P̃(ψ(x))(A(x)b) − A(x)b. For x ∈ V₀, ψ(x) ∈ M ∩ O (step 4), so P̃(ψ(x)) = P_{ψ(x)} is the orthogonal projection onto range A(x), which contains A(x)b; hence F ≡ 0 on the open neighbourhood V₀ of x₀, and DF(x₀) = 0. P̃ ∘ ψ is differentiable at x₀ with derivative L₀ ∘ A(x₀) (chain rule), and x ↦ A(x)b is differentiable at x₀ with derivative a′ ↦ D²ψ(x₀)[a′, b]. By the product rule for applying an operator-valued map to a vector-valued map (HasFDerivAt.clm_apply): 0 = DF(x₀)a = L₀(A(x₀)a)(A(x₀)b) + P̃(y₀)(D²ψ(x₀)[a, b]) − D²ψ(x₀)[a, b]. Since P̃(y₀) = P_{y₀}, L₀(A(x₀)a)(A(x₀)b) = D²ψ(x₀)[a, b] − P_{y₀} D²ψ(x₀)[a, b] = normalPart M y₀ (D²ψ(x₀)[a, b]).
9. By steps 7 and 8 (with η := A(x₀)b): secondFundamentalForm M (ψ x₀) (fderiv ℝ ψ x₀ a) (fderiv ℝ ψ x₀ b) = L₀(A(x₀)a)(A(x₀)b) = normalPart M (ψ x₀) (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ ψ) x₀ a b). As x₀ ∈ V and a, b ∈ ℝⁿ were arbitrary, the theorem follows. (No case distinction on n is needed; for n = 0 both sides are 0.)
proof_key_steps: P_{ψ(x)} = Π(Dψ(x)) with Π(A) = A(A*A)⁻¹A* smooth on injective maps (by TH1).

subproblem.title: Local divergence identity in a C² chart
subproblem.statement: Assume (TH). (TH) is the frozen statement of the sibling root.submanifold_tangent-a1, taken as an explicit hypothesis: (TH1) for every Simon local representation (V, W, ψ) of class r ≥ 1 of any M ⊆ ℝᴺ, tangentSpace M (ψ x) = range Dψ(x) for x ∈ V; (TH2) every n-dimensional C^r Simon submanifold of ℝᴺ is a measurable set on which y ↦ tangentProjection M y is continuous. Let (V, W, ψ) be a Simon local representation of class 2 of M ⊆ ℝᴺ (ψ : ℝⁿ → ℝᴺ) and Y : ℝᴺ → ℝᴺ of class C¹. Then there is w : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ, C¹ on V, with w(x) = 0 for every x ∈ V such that Y(ψ(x)) = 0, and trace Dw(x) = Jψ(x) · (div_M Y(ψ(x)) + ⟨Y(ψ(x)), H(ψ(x))⟩) for every x ∈ V, where Jψ(x) = Chapter02.areaJacobianAt ψ x = √det(Dψ(x)* Dψ(x)), div_M Y = tangentialDivergence M Y and H = meanCurvature M.
subproblem.lean_statement: ((∀ (n N : ℕ) (r : ℕ∞) (M : Set (Rn N)) (V : Set (Rn n)) (W : Set (Rn N)) (ψ : Rn n → Rn N), 1 ≤ r → Chapter02.IsSimonLocalRepresentation r M V W ψ → ∀ x ∈ V, tangentSpace M (ψ x) = LinearMap.range (fderiv ℝ ψ x).toLinearMap) ∧ ∀ (n N : ℕ) (r : ℕ∞) (M : Set (Rn N)), Chapter02.IsSimonSubmanifold (E := Rn n) r M → MeasurableSet M ∧ ContinuousOn (tangentProjection M) M) → ∀ (n N : ℕ) (M : Set (Rn N)) (V : Set (Rn n)) (W : Set (Rn N)) (ψ : Rn n → Rn N) (Y : Rn N → Rn N), Chapter02.IsSimonLocalRepresentation 2 M V W ψ → ContDiff ℝ 1 Y → ∃ w : Rn n → Rn n, ContDiffOn ℝ 1 w V ∧ (∀ x ∈ V, Y (ψ x) = 0 → w x = 0) ∧ ∀ x ∈ V, LinearMap.trace ℝ (Rn n) (fderiv ℝ w x).toLinearMap = Chapter02.areaJacobianAt ψ x * (tangentialDivergence M Y (ψ x) + inner ℝ (Y (ψ x)) (meanCurvature M (ψ x)))
subproblem.natural_proof:
(TH) denotes the frozen statement of the sibling node root.submanifold_tangent-a1 (Submission.simon_submanifold_tangent_basics), taken here as an explicit hypothesis: (TH1) for all n, N, r ≥ 1, M ⊆ ℝᴺ and every Simon local representation (V, W, ψ) of M of class r, tangentSpace M (ψ x) = range Dψ(x) for every x ∈ V; (TH2) every n-dimensional C^r Simon submanifold M of ℝᴺ is a measurable set and y ↦ tangentProjection M y is continuous on M.
Notation. ℝ^d := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) (= Rn d); Hⁿ := μHE[n]. A chart of class r of M is a triple (V, W, ψ) with Chapter02.IsSimonLocalRepresentation r M V W ψ: V ⊆ ℝⁿ and W ⊆ ℝᴺ open, ψ C^r on V, ψ injective on V, ψ(V) = W ∩ M, ψ relatively proper (V ∩ ψ⁻¹(K) is compact for every compact K ⊆ W) and Dψ(x) injective for x ∈ V. For y ∈ M: T_y := tangentSpace M y, P_y := tangentProjection M y (orthogonal projection onto T_y), v^⊥ := normalPart M y v = v − P_y v, τ_i := tangentFrame M y i (an orthonormal basis of T_y), B_y(τ, η) := secondFundamentalForm M y τ η = (fderivWithin ℝ (tangentProjection M) M y τ) η, H(y) := meanCurvature M y = Σ_i B_y(τ_i, τ_i), div_M Y(y) := tangentialDivergence M Y y = Σ_i ⟨τ_i, DY(y)τ_i⟩, and D²ψ(x)[a, b] := fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ ψ) x a b (the derivative at x in direction a of x′ ↦ Dψ(x′)b).

Source: parent proof II.1 step 1, the local identity behind Simon 4.29-4.30 and the divergence theorem 4.21/4.22(*), which the book states without proof. Printed context (Simon p. 61): with X = X^T + X^⊥, X^⊥ = Σ_α (ν^α · X) ν^α, one has div_M X^⊥ = Σ_α (ν^α · X) div_M ν^α = −X · H (4.28, 4.29), and ∫_M div_M X^T = 0 for compactly supported tangential X (4.22(*)). In a chart these two facts combine into the single identity (div_M Y + ⟨Y, H⟩) Jψ = div(Jψ a), proved here.

Setting. Assume (TH). (V, W, ψ) is a chart of class 2 of M ⊆ ℝᴺ (ψ : ℝⁿ → ℝᴺ) and Y : ℝᴺ → ℝᴺ is C¹. Notation on V: A(x) := Dψ(x) (C¹ on V, injective), G := A*A (C¹, symmetric, invertible), J(x) := areaJacobianAt ψ x = normDet A(x) = √det G(x) (SimonGMT areaJacobianAt_eq_sqrt_det_adjoint_comp), u := Y ∘ ψ (C¹ on V), a := G⁻¹ A* u : V → ℝⁿ, u^⊥ := u − A a, S(v, v′) := D²ψ(x)[v, v′] = fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ ψ) x v v′ (symmetric by ContDiffAt.isSymmSndFDerivAt, ψ ∈ C²), e_1, …, e_n the standard orthonormal basis of ℝⁿ, g^{kl} := ⟨e_k, G⁻¹ e_l⟩, ∂_kψ := A e_k. Define w(x) := J(x) • a(x) for x ∈ V and w(x) := 0 for x ∉ V. For a linear map Λ of ℝⁿ, trace Λ = Σ_l ⟨e_l, Λ e_l⟩ (LinearMap.trace_eq_sum_inner).

1. (Regularity and support.) G is positive definite (A injective), so det G > 0 on V; det G is C¹ and √ is smooth on (0, ∞), so J is C¹ on V. Inversion is smooth on invertible operators, so G⁻¹ is C¹ on V; the adjoint is a linear isometry; u is C¹ (chain rule). Hence a and w = J a are C¹ on V. If Y(ψ(x)) = 0 then u(x) = 0, a(x) = 0 and w(x) = 0. This proves the first two conjuncts. Since V is open, fderiv ℝ w x is the derivative of w = J a at x ∈ V.
2. (Projection.) By (TH1), T_{ψ(x)} = range A(x), and A G⁻¹ A* is the orthogonal projection onto range A (G invertible; A G⁻¹ A* is self-adjoint, idempotent, fixes range A and kills (range A)^⊥). Hence P_{ψ(x)} = A G⁻¹ A*, P_{ψ(x)} u = A a, and u^⊥ = normalPart M (ψ x) (u x). Consequently A* u^⊥ = A* u − G G⁻¹ A* u = 0 on V.
3. (Tangential divergence in the chart.) For y = ψ(x) and every linear L of ℝᴺ, Σ_i ⟨τ_i, L τ_i⟩ = trace(L ∘ P_y) for every orthonormal basis (τ_i) of T_y (SimonGMT submanifoldDivergenceAt_eq_sum_inner, applied to the basis tangentFrame M y). With L = DY(y) and P_y = A G⁻¹ A*: div_M Y(y) = trace(DY(y) A G⁻¹ A*) = trace(G⁻¹ A* DY(y) A) (cyclicity of the trace, LinearMap.trace_comp_comm') = trace(G⁻¹ A* Du(x)), because Du(x) = DY(ψ(x)) A(x) (chain rule).
4. (Differentiating u = A a + u^⊥.) For v ∈ ℝⁿ: Du[v] = S(v, a) + A Da[v] + Du^⊥[v] (product rule; the derivative of x ↦ A(x)c in direction v, c fixed, is S(v, c)). Applying G⁻¹ A* and G⁻¹ A* A = I: G⁻¹ A* Du[v] = G⁻¹ A* S(v, a) + Da[v] + G⁻¹ A* Du^⊥[v].
5. (Differentiating A* u^⊥ = 0.) For v ∈ ℝⁿ: (D_v A)* u^⊥ + A* Du^⊥[v] = 0, where (D_v A)* u^⊥ is the vector of ℝⁿ with k-th coordinate ⟨S(v, e_k), u^⊥⟩. Hence G⁻¹ A* Du^⊥[v] = −G⁻¹ Σ_k ⟨S(v, e_k), u^⊥⟩ e_k.
6. (Traces.) Taking the traces of the linear maps v ↦ (each term of step 4) and using step 3: div_M Y(ψ(x)) = T₁ + div a + T₃, where div a := trace Da(x), T₁ := trace(v ↦ G⁻¹ A* S(v, a)) = Σ_l ⟨A G⁻¹ e_l, S(e_l, a)⟩ = Σ_{k,l} g^{kl} ⟨∂_kψ, S(e_l, a)⟩, and T₃ := trace(v ↦ −G⁻¹ Σ_k ⟨S(v, e_k), u^⊥⟩ e_k) = −Σ_{k,l} g^{lk} ⟨S(e_l, e_k), u^⊥⟩ = −⟨u^⊥, Σ_{k,l} g^{kl} S(e_k, e_l)⟩.
7. (Jacobi's formula.) For v ∈ ℝⁿ: D_v(det G) = det G · trace(G⁻¹ D_v G) and D_v G = S(v, ·)* A + A* S(v, ·), where S(v, ·) is the linear map v′ ↦ S(v, v′). Since trace(G⁻¹ S(v, ·)* A) = trace((G⁻¹ S(v, ·)* A)*) = trace(A* S(v, ·) G⁻¹) = trace(G⁻¹ A* S(v, ·)), we get D_v det G = 2 det G · trace(G⁻¹ A* S(v, ·)), hence D_v J = D_v √det G = J · trace(G⁻¹ A* S(v, ·)) = J Σ_{k,l} g^{kl} ⟨∂_kψ, S(v, e_l)⟩. With v = a(x) and the symmetry S(a, e_l) = S(e_l, a): DJ(x)[a(x)] = J(x) · T₁.
8. (Mean curvature in the chart.) Let y = ψ(x), τ_i := tangentFrame M y i (an orthonormal basis of T_y = range A(x), with n elements) and a_i := A(x)⁻¹ τ_i. By the sibling sff_chart, B_y(τ_i, τ_i) = (S(a_i, a_i))^⊥, so H(y) = (Σ_i S(a_i, a_i))^⊥. The a_i form a basis of ℝⁿ orthonormal for (u, v) ↦ ⟨G u, v⟩, so u = Σ_i ⟨G a_i, u⟩ a_i for all u; with u = G⁻¹ e_l this gives G⁻¹ e_l = Σ_i ⟨a_i, e_l⟩ a_i and g^{kl} = Σ_i ⟨e_k, a_i⟩⟨e_l, a_i⟩, whence Σ_i S(a_i, a_i) = Σ_{k,l} g^{kl} S(e_k, e_l) by bilinearity. Because v ↦ v^⊥ = (I − P_y)v is self-adjoint, ⟨Y(y), H(y)⟩ = ⟨u, (Σ_{k,l} g^{kl} S(e_k, e_l))^⊥⟩ = ⟨u^⊥, Σ_{k,l} g^{kl} S(e_k, e_l)⟩ = −T₃.
9. (Conclusion.) By steps 6-8, div_M Y(ψ(x)) = DJ(x)[a(x)]/J(x) + div a − ⟨Y(ψ(x)), H(ψ(x))⟩. Multiplying by J(x) > 0: J (div_M Y(ψ x) + ⟨Y(ψ x), H(ψ x)⟩) = DJ[a] + J div a = trace D(J a)(x), by the product rule D(J a)[v] = (D_v J) a + J Da[v], whose trace is DJ[a] + J trace Da. Since w = J a on the open set V, LinearMap.trace ℝ ℝⁿ (fderiv ℝ w x) = areaJacobianAt ψ x · (tangentialDivergence M Y (ψ x) + ⟨Y(ψ x), meanCurvature M (ψ x)⟩) for every x ∈ V, the third conjunct. (No case distinction on n is needed; for n = 0 both sides are 0.)
proof_key_steps: On V put A = Dψ, G = A*A, J = √det G = areaJacobianAt ψ, u = Y∘ψ, a = G⁻¹A*u, w = J a (C¹ on V, zero where Y∘ψ = 0).
P_{ψ(x)} = AG⁻¹A* (TH1), so div_M Y∘ψ = trace(G⁻¹A*Du), u = Aa + u^⊥ and A*u^⊥ = 0.
Differentiating u = Aa + u^⊥ and A*u^⊥ = 0 and tracing: div_M Y∘ψ = T₁ + div a − ⟨u^⊥, Σg^{kl}D²ψ[e_k,e_l]⟩.
Jacobi's formula gives D_aJ = J·T₁; sff_chart gives ⟨Y,H⟩∘ψ = ⟨u^⊥, Σg^{kl}D²ψ[e_k,e_l]⟩; hence trace Dw = J(div_M Y + ⟨Y,H⟩)∘ψ.

By (TH1), T_y = range Dψ(x), so every τ, η ∈ T_y can be written τ = Dψ(x)a, η = Dψ(x)b with a, b ∈ ℝⁿ. 2. (Normality.) For w ∈ ℝᴺ and v ∈ T_y: ⟨w^⊥, v⟩ = ⟨w, v⟩ − ⟨P_y w, v⟩ = ⟨w, v⟩ − ⟨w, P_y v⟩ = 0, because P_y is self-adjoint and P_y v = v. With w = S_x(a, b), (*) gives ⟨B_y(τ, η), v⟩ = 0 for every v ∈ T_y. Steps 1 and 2 prove the first conjunct.

For x′ ∈ V, ψ(x′) ∈ M and Dψ(x′)b ∈ range Dψ(x′) = T_{ψ(x′)} (TH1), hence f(x′) := ⟨Y(ψ(x′)), Dψ(x′)b⟩ = 0 for all x′ in the open neighbourhood V of x, and therefore Df(x) = 0. f is differentiable at x: Y ∘ ψ is (chain rule; Y is differentiable at ψ(x) = y and ψ at x), and x′ ↦ Dψ(x′)b is (ψ is C² on the open set V). By the product rule for the inner product (HasFDerivAt.inner): 0 = Df(x)a = ⟨DY(y) Dψ(x)a, Dψ(x)b⟩ + ⟨Y(y), S_x(a, b)⟩. Write S_x(a, b) = (S_x(a, b))^⊥ + P_y S_x(a, b); since P_y S_x(a, b) ∈ T_y and Y(y) ⊥ T_y, ⟨Y(y), S_x(a, b)⟩ = ⟨Y(y), (S_x(a, b))^⊥⟩ = ⟨Y(y), B_y(τ, η)⟩ by (*). The vectors a_i form a basis of ℝⁿ that is orthonormal for the inner product (u, v) ↦ ⟨G u, v⟩ = ⟨A u, A v⟩; hence every u ∈ ℝⁿ satisfies u = Σ_i ⟨G a_i, u⟩ a_i. Applying this to u = G⁻¹ e_l and using G* = G gives G⁻¹ e_l = Σ_i ⟨a_i, e_l⟩ a_i, hence g^{kl} = ⟨e_k, G⁻¹ e_l⟩ = Σ_i ⟨e_k, a_i⟩⟨e_l, a_i⟩. By bilinearity of S_x, Σ_i S_x(a_i, a_i) = Σ_{k,l} (Σ_i ⟨e_k, a_i⟩⟨e_l, a_i⟩) S_x(e_k, e_l) = w(x). Finally w(x)^⊥ = w(x) − P_y w(x) = h(x).

(Continuity of H.) h is continuous on V: A is continuous on V (ψ ∈ C¹), G and G⁻¹ are continuous (inversion is continuous on invertible operators), x ↦ S_x = D²ψ(x) is continuous on V (ψ ∈ C² on the open V), and Π is continuous on the open set of injective maps. By SimonGMT IsSimonLocalRepresentation.isEmbedding_chartMap, ψ restricts to a homeomorphism of V onto W ∩ M; hence H = h ∘ (ψ|_V)⁻¹ is continuous on W ∩ M. Given y₀ ∈ M, choose such a chart with y₀ ∈ W; H restricted to M ∩ W is continuous at y₀ and W is a neighbourhood of y₀, so H is continuous within M at y₀ (continuousWithinAt_inter). Hence ContinuousOn (meanCurvature M) M, the second conjunct.

Setting. Assume (TH) [(TH1): T_{ψ(x)} = range Dψ(x) for charts; (TH2): every C^r Simon submanifold is measurable and y ↦ P_y is continuous on it]. M is an n-dimensional C² Simon submanifold of ℝᴺ, Y : ℝᴺ → ℝᴺ is C¹, S ⊆ ℝᴺ is closed, Y = 0 off S, and M ∩ S is compact. Hⁿ := μHE[n]; div_M Ỹ := tangentialDivergence M Ỹ; H := meanCurvature M.

0. (Preliminary facts.)
 (a) M is measurable and y ↦ P_y is continuous on M (TH2); H is continuous on M (sibling sff_properties, second conjunct).
 (b) For y ∈ M and every linear L of ℝᴺ, Σ_i ⟨τ_i, L τ_i⟩ = trace(L ∘ P_y) for every orthonormal basis (τ_i) of T_y (SimonGMT submanifoldDivergenceAt_eq_sum_inner with the basis tangentFrame M y). Hence for every C¹ field Ỹ, div_M Ỹ(y) = trace(DỸ(y) ∘ P_y) for y ∈ M, a continuous function of y on M (DỸ continuous, P continuous on M, composition and trace continuous). Also div_M(Ỹ₁ + Ỹ₂)(y) = div_M Ỹ₁(y) + div_M Ỹ₂(y) when Ỹ₁, Ỹ₂ are differentiable at y (fderiv_add), and similarly for finite sums.
 (c) If a C¹ field Ỹ vanishes outside a closed set F and y ∉ F, then Ỹ ≡ 0 on the open neighbourhood Fᶜ of y, so Ỹ(y) = 0, DỸ(y) = 0, div_M Ỹ(y) = 0 and ⟨Ỹ(y), H(y)⟩ = 0.
 (d) If F is such that M ∩ F is compact, then Hⁿ(M ∩ F) < ∞ (sibling measure_bounds, part (a)).
1. (Integrability.) Let Ỹ be C¹ and F closed with Ỹ = 0 off F and M ∩ F compact. Then f₁ := div_M Ỹ and f₂ := ⟨Ỹ, H⟩ are continuous on M (0(a), 0(b)), vanish on M ∖ F (0(c)), and are bounded on the compact set M ∩ F (IsCompact.exists_bound_of_continuousOn), so |f_i| ≤ C · 1_{M∩F} on M. Each f_i is a.e.-strongly measurable for Hⁿ restricted to M (ContinuousOn.aestronglyMeasurable on the measurable set M), and ∫_M |f_i| dHⁿ ≤ C · Hⁿ(M ∩ F) < ∞ (0(d)). Hence f₁ and f₂ are integrable on M. With Ỹ := Y and F := S this proves the first two conjuncts.
2. (Localized identity.) Let (V, W, ψ) be a chart of M of class 2 and ζ : ℝᴺ → ℝ a C^∞ function with compact support and K_ζ := tsupport ζ ⊆ W. Put Ỹ := ζ Y (C¹) and f := div_M Ỹ + ⟨Ỹ, H⟩. Claim: ∫_M f dHⁿ = 0.
 2a. Ỹ vanishes off the closed set K_ζ, and M ∩ K_ζ = ψ(V ∩ ψ⁻¹(K_ζ)) is compact (relative properness, continuity of ψ on V, K_ζ ⊆ W and W ∩ M = ψ(V)). By step 1, f is integrable on M; by 0(c), f = 0 on M ∖ K_ζ ⊇ M ∖ ψ(V) (because M ∖ ψ(V) = M ∖ W). Since M is measurable (TH2), ψ(V) = W ∩ M ⊆ M is measurable, and f = 0 on M ∖ ψ(V), ∫_M f = ∫_{ψ(V)} f (MeasureTheory.setIntegral_eq_of_subset_of_forall_sdiff_eq_zero with t := M, s := ψ(V)).
 2b. (Area formula.) By SimonGMT integral_area_formula_of_injective_derivative (s := V measurable; ψ differentiable at every x ∈ V; Dψ(x) injective; ψ injective on V) and finrank ℝ ℝⁿ = n: ∫_{ψ(V)} f dHⁿ = ∫_V Jψ(x) · f(ψ(x)) dHⁿ(x), where Jψ = areaJacobianAt ψ and μHE[n] on ℝⁿ is an additive Haar measure (it equals Lebesgue measure, EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume).

2. (Zero first variation.) Let K and φ satisfy IsAdmissibleDeformation 2 U K φ (so K is compact and K ⊆ U). We show HasDerivAt (deformedArea n M K φ) 0 0.

4. Case U ∩ M ≠ ∅. M ⊆ ℝ^{n+ℓ} is an n-dimensional C² Simon submanifold, U is open, and IsStationaryIn n M U, i.e. (S1) μHE[n](M ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U, and (S2) HasDerivAt (deformedArea n M K φ) 0 0 whenever IsAdmissibleDeformation 2 U K φ. Hⁿ := μHE[n], H := meanCurvature M.

1. Fix y₀ ∈ M ∩ U and suppose, for a contradiction, that H(y₀) ≠ 0. Let e := H(y₀) and c₀ := ‖H(y₀)‖²/2 > 0.

Choose ρ > 0 with 2ρ < δ and B̄(y₀, 2ρ) ⊆ U ∩ W (U ∩ W is an open set containing y₀). For y ∈ M ∩ B̄(y₀, 2ρ), by Cauchy-Schwarz: ⟨e, H(y)⟩ = ‖H(y₀)‖² + ⟨H(y₀), H(y) − H(y₀)⟩ ≥ ‖H(y₀)‖² − ‖H(y₀)‖ · ‖H(y₀)‖/2 = c₀.

Let Y(x) := ζ(x) • e. Then Y is C^∞ (in particular C²), HasCompactSupport Y, and tsupport Y ⊆ tsupport ζ = S ⊆ U.
5. By the sibling scaled_deformation there is c > 0 such that φ t x := x + (c t) • Y(x) satisfies IsAdmissibleDeformation 2 U K φ with K := tsupport Y, and initialVelocity φ x = c • Y(x) for all x, i.e. initialVelocity φ = (x ↦ c • Y(x)).

FirstVariation applies: M is a C¹ Simon submanifold (1 ≤ 1, and each class-2 chart is a class-1 chart because ContDiffOn ℝ 2 implies ContDiffOn ℝ 1); U is open; y₀ ∈ U ∩ M; for compact K′ ⊆ U, μHE[n](K′ ∩ M) = μHE[n](M ∩ K′) < ∞ by (S1); φ is admissible of class 2. It gives HasDerivAt (deformedArea n M K φ) (∫_M div_M(initialVelocity φ) dHⁿ) 0. By uniqueness of derivatives (HasDerivAt.unique), ∫_M div_M(c • Y) dHⁿ = 0.

M ∩ B is measurable (M is measurable by (TH2), B is open) and Hⁿ(M ∩ B) ≤ Hⁿ(M ∩ S) < ∞. As f is integrable and nonnegative on M: ∫_M f ≥ ∫_{M ∩ B} f ≥ c c₀ · Hⁿ(M ∩ B) (MeasureTheory.setIntegral_mono_set, then the constant lower bound on a set of finite measure).
9. By sibling measure_bounds (b) (y₀ ∈ M, B open, y₀ ∈ B), Hⁿ(M ∩ B) > 0, and it is finite; so ∫_M f ≥ c c₀ Hⁿ(M ∩ B) > 0, contradicting step 7. Hence H(y₀) = 0. As y₀ ∈ M ∩ U was arbitrary, meanCurvature M y = 0 for all y ∈ M ∩ U.
proof_key_steps: If H(y₀) ≠ 0, continuity of H on M gives ⟨H(y₀), H⟩ ≥ c₀ > 0 on M ∩ B̄(y₀,2ρ) with B̄(y₀,2ρ) ⊆ U ∩ W, and M ∩ B̄(y₀,2ρ) is compact by chart properness.
With a bump ζ and Y = ζH(y₀), the deformation x + ctY(x) is admissible with velocity cY (scaled_deformation).
Stationarity, FirstVariation and uniqueness of derivatives give ∫_M div_M(cY) = 0; the divergence identity gives ∫_M cζ⟨H(y₀),H⟩ = 0.
The integrand is ≥ 0 on M and ≥ c·c₀ on M ∩ B(y₀,ρ), which has positive finite Hⁿ-measure (measure_bounds): contradiction.

subproblem.title: Second variation of a stationary submanifold along normal deformations (Simon 5.11, C³ correction)
subproblem.statement: Assume (TH), FirstVariation and SecondVariation (the two conjuncts proved by the sibling root.variation_formulas-a1). (TH) is the frozen statement of the sibling root.submanifold_tangent-a1, taken as an explicit hypothesis: (TH1) for every Simon local representation (V, W, ψ) of class r ≥ 1 of any M ⊆ ℝᴺ, tangentSpace M (ψ x) = range Dψ(x) for x ∈ V; (TH2) every n-dimensional C^r Simon submanifold of ℝᴺ is a measurable set on which y ↦ tangentProjection M y is continuous. Then SecondVariationStationary holds: if M ⊆ ℝ^{n+ℓ} is an n-dimensional C² Simon submanifold, U open with (closure M ∖ M) ∩ U = ∅, M stationary in U, and φ admissible of class 3 for (U, K) with initial velocity X normal to M (⟨X(y), v⟩ = 0 for y ∈ M, v ∈ T_yM), then t ↦ (μHE[n](φ_t(M ∩ K))).toReal (deformedArea n M K φ) is differentiable near 0 and its derivative has derivative ∫_M (Σ_i |(D_{τ_i}X)^⊥|² − Σ_{i,j} (X · B(τ_i, τ_j))²) dμHE[n] (stableSecondVariationIntegrand) at 0.
subproblem.lean_statement: ((∀ (n N : ℕ) (r : ℕ∞) (M : Set (Rn N)) (V : Set (Rn n)) (W : Set (Rn N)) (ψ : Rn n → Rn N), 1 ≤ r → Chapter02.IsSimonLocalRepresentation r M V W ψ → ∀ x ∈ V, tangentSpace M (ψ x) = LinearMap.range (fderiv ℝ ψ x).toLinearMap) ∧ ∀ (n N : ℕ) (r : ℕ∞) (M : Set (Rn N)), Chapter02.IsSimonSubmanifold (E := Rn n) r M → MeasurableSet M ∧ ContinuousOn (tangentProjection M) M) → FirstVariation → SecondVariation → SecondVariationStationary
subproblem.natural_proof:
(TH) denotes the frozen statement of the sibling node root.submanifold_tangent-a1 (Submission.simon_submanifold_tangent_basics), taken here as an explicit hypothesis: (TH1) for all n, N, r ≥ 1, M ⊆ ℝᴺ and every Simon local representation (V, W, ψ) of M of class r, tangentSpace M (ψ x) = range Dψ(x) for every x ∈ V; (TH2) every n-dimensional C^r Simon submanifold M of ℝᴺ is a measurable set and y ↦ tangentProjection M y is continuous on M.
Notation. ℝ^d := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) (= Rn d); Hⁿ := μHE[n]. A chart of class r of M is a triple (V, W, ψ) with Chapter02.IsSimonLocalRepresentation r M V W ψ: V ⊆ ℝⁿ and W ⊆ ℝᴺ open, ψ C^r on V, ψ injective on V, ψ(V) = W ∩ M, ψ relatively proper (V ∩ ψ⁻¹(K) is compact for every compact K ⊆ W) and Dψ(x) injective for x ∈ V. For y ∈ M: T_y := tangentSpace M y, P_y := tangentProjection M y (orthogonal projection onto T_y), v^⊥ := normalPart M y v = v − P_y v, τ_i := tangentFrame M y i (an orthonormal basis of T_y), B_y(τ, η) := secondFundamentalForm M y τ η = (fderivWithin ℝ (tangentProjection M) M y τ) η, H(y) := meanCurvature M y = Σ_i B_y(τ_i, τ_i), div_M Y(y) := tangentialDivergence M Y y = Σ_i ⟨τ_i, DY(y)τ_i⟩, and D²ψ(x)[a, b] := fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ ψ) x a b (the derivative at x in direction a of x′ ↦ Dψ(x′)b).

Source: Simon, Ch. 2, Lemma 5.11 (p. 65), with the C³ correction of the README errata (5.4 and 5.11 use deformations of class C³). Printed proof: "First we note that ∫_M div_M Z dHⁿ = 0 by virtue of the fact that M is stationary in U, and div_M X = −X · H = 0 by virtue of 4.29 and 5.5(2) and the fact that X is normal to M. The proof is then completed by noting that τ_i · D_{τ_j}X = −X · B(τ_i, τ_j) by virtue of 4.24 and the fact that X is normal to M." The detailed argument below is parent proof II.3 (steps 8-12); the localisation of parent step 9 is replaced by the sibling stationary_mean_zero, which proves "stationary ⇒ H = 0 on M ∩ U" for arbitrary open U by the same argument (parent II.2 steps 6-7).

Setting. Assume (TH), FirstVariation and SecondVariation. Unfold SecondVariationStationary: let n, ℓ ∈ ℕ, M, U, K ⊆ ℝ^{n+ℓ} and φ : ℝ → ℝ^{n+ℓ} → ℝ^{n+ℓ} with M an n-dimensional C² Simon submanifold, U open, (closure M ∖ M) ∩ U = ∅, IsStationaryIn n M U, IsAdmissibleDeformation 3 U K φ, and X := initialVelocity φ normal to M: ⟨X(y), v⟩ = 0 for y ∈ M, v ∈ T_y. Let Z := initialAcceleration φ, A := deformedArea n M K φ, τ_i := tangentFrame M y i, B_y := secondFundamentalForm M y, H := meanCurvature M, Hⁿ := μHE[n].

1. (Regularity.) K is compact and K ⊆ U. By sibling deformation_regularity (second conjunct), X is C² and Z is C¹ on ℝ^{n+ℓ}, and X = Z = 0 off K. Since Kᶜ is open, X and Z vanish on a neighbourhood of every y ∉ K, so DX(y) = DZ(y) = 0 for y ∉ K.
2. (Compactness and finiteness.) M ∩ K is compact: if y_k ∈ M ∩ K and y_k → y, then y ∈ K ⊆ U (K is closed) and y ∈ closure M; since (closure M ∖ M) ∩ U = ∅, y ∈ M. So M ∩ K is a closed subset of the compact set K. By the first conjunct of IsStationaryIn, Hⁿ(M ∩ K) < ∞.
3. (H = 0 on M ∩ U.) By sibling stationary_mean_zero (hypotheses (TH), FirstVariation, M C², U open, M stationary in U), H(y) = 0 for every y ∈ M ∩ U.
4. (∫_M div_M Z = 0.) By sibling divergence_identity (Y := Z ∈ C¹, S := K closed, Z = 0 off K, M ∩ K compact), div_M Z is integrable on M and ∫_M div_M Z = −∫_M ⟨Z, H⟩. For y ∈ M, ⟨Z(y), H(y)⟩ = 0 (if y ∈ U, H(y) = 0 by step 3; if y ∉ U, then y ∉ K and Z(y) = 0). Hence ∫_M div_M Z dHⁿ = 0. (This is the printed "∫_M div_M Z dHⁿ = 0 by virtue of the fact that M is stationary in U".)
5. (Pointwise identity.) For every y ∈ M: secondVariationIntegrand M φ y = div_M Z(y) + stableSecondVariationIntegrand M φ y.
 (a) y ∈ M ∖ K: X(y) = 0, DX(y) = 0 and DZ(y) = 0 (step 1), so div_M Z(y) = 0, div_M X(y) = 0, normalPart M y (DX(y) τ_i) = 0, ⟨τ_i, DX(y) τ_j⟩ = 0 and ⟨X(y), B_y(τ_i, τ_j)⟩ = 0 for all i, j; both sides are 0.
 (b) y ∈ M ∩ K ⊆ M ∩ U: X is differentiable at y (C²) and normal along M, so by sibling sff_properties (third conjunct), for all i, j: (**) ⟨τ_j, DX(y) τ_i⟩ = −⟨X(y), B_y(τ_i, τ_j)⟩. [(**) actually holds at every y ∈ M, since X is C² everywhere and normal along M; the case split (a)/(b) is only used to know H(y) = 0, which needs y ∈ U.] Hence div_M X(y) = Σ_i ⟨τ_i, DX(y) τ_i⟩ = −⟨X(y), Σ_i B_y(τ_i, τ_i)⟩ = −⟨X(y), H(y)⟩ = 0 by step 3 (the printed "div_M X = −X · H = 0"). Using (**) twice and the symmetry B_y(τ_j, τ_i) = B_y(τ_i, τ_j) (sff_properties, first conjunct): ⟨τ_i, DX(y) τ_j⟩ ⟨τ_j, DX(y) τ_i⟩ = ⟨X(y), B_y(τ_j, τ_i)⟩ ⟨X(y), B_y(τ_i, τ_j)⟩ = ⟨X(y), B_y(τ_i, τ_j)⟩² (the printed "τ_i · D_{τ_j}X = −X · B(τ_i, τ_j)"). Substituting into secondVariationIntegrand = div_M Z + (div_M X)² + Σ_i |(DX τ_i)^⊥|² − Σ_{i,j} ⟨τ_i, DX τ_j⟩⟨τ_j, DX τ_i⟩ gives div_M Z(y) + Σ_i |(DX(y) τ_i)^⊥|² − Σ_{i,j} ⟨X(y), B_y(τ_i, τ_j)⟩² = div_M Z(y) + stableSecondVariationIntegrand M φ y.
6. (Integrability of the stable integrand.) For y ∈ M let F(y) := trace(P_y DX(y)* (I − P_y) DX(y) P_y) − trace(P_y DX(y)* P_y DX(y) P_y). For any orthonormal basis (τ_i) of T_y and linear L, Σ_i ⟨τ_i, L τ_i⟩ = trace(P_y L P_y). Hence Σ_i ‖(DX(y) τ_i)^⊥‖² = Σ_i ⟨τ_i, DX(y)* (I − P_y) DX(y) τ_i⟩ (I − P_y is a self-adjoint idempotent) = trace(P_y DX(y)* (I − P_y) DX(y) P_y); and, by (**) for y ∈ M ∩ K and trivially for y ∈ M ∖ K (both sides 0), Σ_{i,j} ⟨X(y), B_y(τ_i, τ_j)⟩² = Σ_{i,j} ⟨τ_j, DX(y) τ_i⟩² = Σ_i ‖P_y DX(y) τ_i‖² = trace(P_y DX(y)* P_y DX(y) P_y). So stableSecondVariationIntegrand M φ = F on M. F is continuous on M (y ↦ P_y is continuous on M by (TH2), DX is continuous, and adjoint, composition and trace are continuous), so the stable integrand is continuous on M and a.e.-strongly measurable for Hⁿ restricted to M (M is measurable by (TH2)). It vanishes on M ∖ K (5(a)) and is bounded on the compact set M ∩ K; as Hⁿ(M ∩ K) < ∞ (step 2), it is integrable on M.
7. (Integral identity.) By step 5 (equality on the measurable set M; setIntegral_congr_fun), the integrability of div_M Z (step 4) and of the stable integrand (step 6), and additivity of the integral: ∫_M secondVariationIntegrand M φ dHⁿ = ∫_M div_M Z dHⁿ + ∫_M stableSecondVariationIntegrand M φ dHⁿ = ∫_M stableSecondVariationIntegrand M φ dHⁿ by step 4.
8. (Case U ∩ M ≠ ∅.) SecondVariation applies: M is a C¹ Simon submanifold (each class-2 chart is a class-1 chart); U is open; U ∩ M ≠ ∅; μHE[n](K′ ∩ M) = μHE[n](M ∩ K′) < ∞ for every compact K′ ⊆ U by IsStationaryIn; φ is admissible of class 3. It yields (∀ᶠ t in 𝓝 0, DifferentiableAt ℝ A t) and HasDerivAt (deriv A) (∫_M secondVariationIntegrand M φ dHⁿ) 0, and by step 7 the value equals ∫_M stableSecondVariationIntegrand M φ dHⁿ.
9. (Case U ∩ M = ∅.) Then M ∩ K ⊆ M ∩ U = ∅, so A(t) = (Hⁿ(φ t '' ∅)).toReal = 0 for every t: A is the zero function, differentiable everywhere, deriv A is the zero function, and HasDerivAt (deriv A) 0 0. Every y ∈ M lies outside U ⊇ K, so by 5(a) the stable integrand vanishes on M and ∫_M stableSecondVariationIntegrand M φ dHⁿ = 0. Hence the conclusion holds in this case too.
10. Steps 8 and 9 prove SecondVariationStationary.
proof_key_steps: X ∈ C², Z ∈ C¹ vanish (with derivatives) off K (deformation_regularity); M ∩ K is compact since (closure M ∖ M) ∩ U = ∅; H = 0 on M ∩ U (stationary_mean_zero).
∫_M div_M Z = −∫_M ⟨Z,H⟩ = 0 (divergence_identity).
Normal-field identity ⟨τ_j,DXτ_i⟩ = −⟨X,B(τ_i,τ_j)⟩ and symmetry of B (sff_properties): div_M X = −⟨X,H⟩ = 0 and secondVariationIntegrand = div_M Z + stableSecondVariationIntegrand on M.
The stable integrand equals a continuous trace expression on M, hence is integrable; SecondVariation (or the trivial case U ∩ M = ∅) gives the result.

audit.reason: The proof establishes compact support, zero acceleration-divergence integral and the exact pointwise integrand identity. Its trace expressions justify integrability without continuous frames. SecondVariation and the empty case then prove the frozen conclusion non-circularly.
